uzo.purpose: Shows the name or a short hint of a control while it is hovered or focused.

instead.kialo: What a person needs to act stands visibly as text — under a field as the kampo's help, elsewhere as running text — because whoever does not hover or focus never sees a tooltip, and on touch there is no hovering.
A layer a person operates — a link, a field, a button in it — is a popover, because a tooltip vanishes when the pointer leaves and takes no focus; the sxvebilo stays and holds the focus.

boundary.kialo: A disabled control takes no focus and on many platforms no hover, so its tooltip is never reached by keyboard; a person decides whether the reason stands visibly beside the control instead.

with.kialo: A button that shows only an icon carries its name as a tooltip, because whoever sees only a picture needs the word visibly too; the tooltip's text is the button's label, heard once.
An icon that carries meaning may show its name on hover, because the word confirms what the sign says; a decorative icon has no tooltip, it says nothing.
